title: Honcho Developer's Guide
subtitle: How Honcho is built, configured, deployed and maintained.

blocks.text: The Five Files
This module is built from five files that work together. Understanding what each one is _for_ — and just as importantly, what it's _not_ for — is the fastest way to orient yourself in this codebase.

rows: The controller. Every action — save, view, delete, manage-list, this help page — is a method here. This is where real security enforcement lives: server-side whitelist stripping, permission checks, database queries. Roughly 8,000 lines; most of it is untouched legacy code from before this module's active development phase (see **Known Issues**).

Thin wrapper around the edit form. Renders the header (photo, name, Save/Cancel buttons — which pair depends on `$_SESSION['actionmode']`), then `include()`s `ccmpcrudcontact.php` for the actual fields. Rarely needs changes on its own.
The real edit form. Every editable field lives here, organized into collapsible sections. This is the file you'll touch most often when adding/moving/re-permissioning a field.

The read-only view — what a member sees when they open "My Profile" before clicking Update. Same field set as the edit form, conceptually, but rendered as plain text via Bootstrap **tabs** (not collapse panels) using an output-buffering trick — see the code comments at the top of the file for how `vf_section_open()`/`vf_section_close()`/`vf_tabs_render()` work together.

The admin list/management view. One unified table (not per-mode duplicates like the original legacy version had), with real SQL `JOIN`s pulling chapter name, address, and member-type label directly rather than translating codes in PHP.

blocks.text: Styling
Tab/section labels and other UI chrome are styled in `custom.css`, not `style.css` and not in any PHP file.

**Font pop-up (2026-10-27):** a **Font** link in the member top bar (`views/navbar.php`, members only) opens a pop-up with the five size choices (Tabs, Headings, Labels, Values, Buttons; Small / Medium / Large from `ccmps_settings`, colour rows left out), filled by `member_font_sizes()` (`utilities_helper.php`). **Save** posts to `welcome-ccmps/savefontsizes` (own record only, session token `fontsize_token`, each id checked against its type, Auditlog `FontSizes`) and reloads the page. Never write a `font-size` inline on the elements the size system styles: it overrides the member's choice.

**The update form too (2026-10-27):** the size rules used to match only the view page's tabs (`.tabs-container`), so the update form (collapsible boxes) ignored them. `cf_section_open()` now marks each box `ccmp-form-section`, and `_with_fontsize_style()` also targets `.ccmp-form-section` (section titles, `h4`, `label`, `.form-control`). `custom.css` lets drop-downs there grow with the text (Bootstrap's `select.form-control:not([size]):not([multiple])` has a fixed height).

**Never add rules to `themes/inspinia/css/style.css` directly.** That's the theme's own vendor file — a future theme update will silently overwrite it, and anything added there goes with it. `custom.css` (loaded via its own `<link>` tag in `inspinia.php`, placed immediately after `style.css`'s so it wins the cascade on anything overlapping) is the correct home for every module-specific style going forward. `style.css` still has some of the previous developer's own hand-edits baked into it from before this project (e.g. a `padding: 1px` change with a comment noting the original value) — those weren't retroactively migrated, so a theme update could still silently lose them; only new work is protected by this convention going forward.
The Font Size Preference System (per-element, per-user)

Five independently-configurable elements — tabs, section headers, field labels, field values, buttons — each with its own small/medium/large choice, per member. This intentionally allows mismatched combinations (e.g. tiny tabs with huge field values); that flexibility was a deliberate choice, not an oversight, partly in anticipation of a future mobile-specific mode where sizes would be preset for what renders best and members wouldn't be allowed to edit them at all.
Two tables work together:

items: `ccmps_settings` — 15 rows: one per (element type × size tier) combination. Columns: `id`, `title` ('small'/'medium'/'large'), `settingvalue` (the actual pixel number), `type` ('tab'/'header'/'label'/'value'/'button'), `description` (the human-readable dropdown label, e.g. "Medium Tabs"). Editable by system_admin via a dedicated CRUD (`managefontsizes()`/`savefontsizesettings()`, linked from the sidemenu) — this is where the actual pixel values for each tier get configured, shared across every member.

`ccmps` — 5 columns (`tab_setting`, `header_setting`, `label_setting`, `value_setting`, `button_setting`), each an FK id into `ccmps_settings`. This is the per-member choice, editable via 5 ordinary dropdowns in Preferences — no modal, no AJAX, just normal form fields saved through the regular `ccmpsubmit()` flow.

blocks.text: **Never hardcode a specific `ccmps_settings` id as "the medium option for type X."** The schema's own column defaults do exactly this (`tab_setting` defaults to `2`, `header_setting` to `5`, and so on — each the middle id of its 3-row block, assuming a specific insert order) — that's acceptable as a database-level fallback, since MySQL `DEFAULT` clauses can only be literal values, not dynamic lookups. But no *application code* should make that same assumption. Every place that needs to resolve "what does this stored id actually mean" — the inline style generator in `inspinia.php`, and the display translation in `_convert_to_user_friendly()` — looks the row up by matching `type` + `title = 'medium'` instead, and only falls back to that lookup if the stored id is missing or its `type` doesn't match what's expected. If `ccmps_settings` ever gets reordered or reseeded, a hardcoded-id assumption would silently point at the wrong type/tier combination with no error anywhere to catch it.
How the CSS actually gets generated

Since the real pixel values are per-user and only knowable at request time, this can't be static CSS at all — it's a small inline `<style>` block, generated directly in `inspinia.php` on every page load. Views in this app render via `include()`, which preserves the calling controller's `$this` — so `inspinia.php` can call `$this->model` directly, the same way `manage.php` and `viewccmp.php` already do inline, without needing every controller action to pre-compute this and pass it through `$data`.
What this replaced
A single-value, session-based system that was genuinely broken in three separate ways, not just outdated:

items: It used the stored font size as an HTML _heading level_ (`<h1>` through `<h6>`) via `<h<?= $_SESSION['fontsize'] ?>>...</h<?= $_SESSION['fontsize'] ?>>`, conflating a user's visual preference with document structure — actively confusing anything relying on heading hierarchy, like screen readers.

Three different places set that same session variable with mutually incompatible conventions: raw numeric passthrough, a self-correcting default, and a `switch` that silently converted the number into word-strings (`'Large'`/`'Medium'`/`'Small'`) — which would have broken the heading-level trick outright if it ran afterward.
A 12+-call-site helper function, `_get_font_sizes()`, referenced `$ccmp_id` before ever assigning it, so its entire database-lookup body was silently dead code the whole time.

blocks.text: All of it — the heading-level trick, the three inconsistent assignment sites, the broken helper function, the standalone Font modal and its AJAX save handler, and the `ccmps.fontsize` column itself — has been fully removed, not just deprecated.
Trongate MVC Conventions

items: Controller methods render a view by setting `$data['view_module']` / `$data['view_file']`, then calling `$this->templates->inspinia($data)`.

**Trongate does not reliably auto-map URL segments to method parameters.** Don't declare `function foo($id)` expecting the framework to populate `$id` from the URL — pull it explicitly with `segment(3)` instead. We found this the hard way: a parameter with no default value (`function updateccmp($retrying)`) threw a fatal `ArgumentCountError` the moment it was called via a plain link, because Trongate called it with zero arguments. Always give parameters a default, or better, don't rely on them at all.

`$this->model->get_where($id, 'table')` returns a single `stdClass` object. `$this->model->get_one_where($col, $val, 'table')` — same shape, matched by an arbitrary column instead of the primary key. `$this->model->query($sql, 'object')` — returns an **array** of row objects, even for a single-row result; you need `$result[0]` to get at it. Mixing these up (assigning object-syntax onto what's actually an array) caused a real fatal crash we had to trace and fix.
`$this->model->get_where_custom($col, $val, '=', $orderCol, 'table')` — used for lookups keyed on something other than the primary key, or when you need every matching row rather than just one.

blocks.text: **The single most common bug class in this codebase:** confusing whether a value is an object (`->`) or an array (`[]`). PHP does _not_ reliably throw a loud, obvious error when you get this wrong — depending on context it can silently no-op, throw a quiet warning, or (for property _assignment_ on an array specifically) throw a genuine fatal `Error`. When something behaves strangely for no obvious reason, checking this mismatch first has paid off repeatedly during this module's development.

**Resolved:** `ccmps.salutation` was originally `varchar(55)` despite the code treating it as an integer FK to `ref_salutations` — since fixed by converting the column to `tinyint(1) DEFAULT 0` directly in the database. If any member record had a pre-existing free-text salutation (like "Mr.") saved before this change, it's worth a quick check that the type conversion didn't silently coerce it to `0` rather than mapping it to the correct `ref_salutations.id` — MySQL will happily do that coercion without erroring, especially outside strict SQL mode.

Showing it: always print `salutation_title($id)` (`utilities_helper.php`), never the column itself; 0 = none. The Directory, Current Roster, Master Roster, export and profile printed the id, so every name read "Smith, 0 John" (fixed 2026-10-28).

Session Variable Scoping Convention

**`ccmps_`-prefixed session variables are scoped to this module only. Unprefixed variables are enterprise-wide, spanning every module.** For example, `$_SESSION['ccmps_system_admin']` is set from `ccmps.system_admin` and grants system-admin rights within the CCMPS module only. `$_SESSION['system_admin']` (no prefix) will be set by the Honcho module, from `honcho_user_accounts`, and grants system-admin rights across _every_ module — Honcho isn't built yet, but this module's code already recognizes it, since an enterprise-wide admin should obviously have full rights here too. Every permission check that involves `system_admin` checks both forms with `||`, for exactly this reason. The same convention applies to future roles: `ccmps_content_admin`/`ccmps_event_admin` will be this module's own content/event management (not yet built); a future unprefixed `library_admin` would control one shared document library across the whole enterprise.
The Core Rule

**A `disabled` HTML attribute is UX polish, not security.** Anyone can remove it via browser dev tools and submit the field anyway. Every permission check that matters is duplicated server-side in `ccmpsubmit()`, which independently strips restricted fields from the save whitelist before anything touches the database — regardless of what the submitted form claims. If you ever add a new restricted field, you MUST add the strip logic in `ccmpsubmit()`, not just hide/disable it in the form. The form-side gating exists purely so the UI doesn't lie to the user about what they can do.

blocks.text: Worked Example: Chapter-Admin Granting
This is the most nuanced permission rule in the module, and a good template for reasoning about any future rule of similar shape:

items: `system_admin` and `ccmp_admin` operate at the **national level** — they can grant Chapter Admin to any member, in any chapter, with no restriction.
A chapter's own `subentity_admin`, or a member whose role is Chapter President, can **only** grant it to a fellow member of their _own_ chapter.

blocks.text: **A real bug we found and fixed here:** `viewccmp.php` receives data _after_ `_convert_to_user_friendly()` has already run, which overwrites `$data['subentity']` with the chapter's _text name_ for display purposes. Comparing that text name against the viewer's raw numeric session id would never match — silently hiding the grant checkbox from every legitimate chapter president, with no error anywhere to indicate why. Fixed by preserving the raw id under a separate `$data['subentity_id']` key before the text translation happens. **Lesson: when a value is going to get "friendly-formatted" for display, always ask whether anything downstream still needs the raw form — and if so, keep both.**
Member Permissions Screen

`welcome-ccmpspermissions/manage` (System Admin menu → Member Permissions, added 2026-10-16) lists members with a checkbox for each super-user flag, so permissions can be seen and set in one place instead of record by record. It opens showing only members who hold a permission; `manage/all` shows every member (deceased and soft-deleted excluded).

items: **Who:** member system admins only, whether or not the Honcho staff module is deployed. The check in `__construct()` reads `system_admin` from the database, not the session, so removing someone's System Admin locks them out of the screen at once. Staff logins are sent back to the Honcho dashboard.

**Columns:** the flags login copies into the session, listed in `_permission_flags()`: `system_admin`, `ccmp_admin`, `subentity_admin`, `student_admin`, `content_admin`, `event_admin` (since 2026-10-20, for the content manager), `financial_admin` (since 2026-10-22: Financial Admins change the Financial tab of System Settings). `library_admin` is on `ccmps` but nothing reads it yet; add it to `_permission_flags()` and `rbac_member_roles()` when something does.

**Saving:** each click posts to `togglepermission()` (AJAX, JSON reply). Since RBAC step 5 (2026-10-18) a tick **joins or leaves the role's Security Group** (`rbac_set_member_role()`: Member System Admins, Member Admins, Chapter Admins, Student Admins, Content Admins, Event Admins) and the `ccmps` column is re-synced from the groups; a role the member also gets from another group can't be removed here (the reply says so). It writes a `GrantPermission`/`RemovePermission` Auditlog entry. Only columns in `_permission_flags()` can be changed, and a per-session token stops other sites posting changes.
**Safety:** you can't remove your own System Admin, and the last System Admin can't be removed.

**When it takes effect:** at that member's next login, because login sets the `ccmps_*` flags from the groups (`rbac_member_session_flags()`). Changing your own flags updates your session straight away.

blocks.text: Member Admin Roles Live in Security Groups

Since RBAC step 5 (2026-10-18) the four member admin roles are Security Groups functions (`ccmps/system_admin`, `member_admin`, `chapter_admin`, `student_admin`). The `ccmps` columns (`system_admin`, `ccmp_admin`, `subentity_admin`, `student_admin`) are kept as a **copy** so existing queries and reports keep working; `rbac_sync_member_columns()` rewrites them after every change. The Member Permissions screen, the Roles & Permissions boxes on the member record (`ccmpsubmit()`) and the Security Groups screens all go through the same helpers, so the three always agree.

items: **Login and refresh** (`Welcome.php`, `refreshmysessiondata()`): the flags are set from the columns, then from the groups when the member has a login row. They also set `ccmps_admin` from `ccmps_ccmp_admin`; the menus check `ccmps_admin`, which nothing used to set, so the Member Admin menu now appears.
**A member with no login row** gets one (`trongate_users`) when given a role; a member who never gets a role doesn't need one. Members with no login row keep column-based flags.

**Deceased members** keep no roles: saving a record with Deceased ticked calls `rbac_clear_member_access()`, which removes the login from every Security Group and clears the four columns (since 2026-10-19; older records were cleared by `2026-10-19-clear-deceased-member-roles.sql`). Soft-deleted members were left out of the groups in step 2, so their columns may still show roles.

Org-specific words come from `config/config.php`: `CCMP` / `CCMPS` (Member/Members), `SUBENTITY` / `SUBENTITIES` (Chapter/Chapters, or Branch, Office…). Screen text uses the constant, never the word: `<?= SUBENTITY ?> Admin` in a view, `SUBENTITY.' Admin'` in PHP, `strtolower(SUBENTITY)` mid-sentence. Visible-but-Disabled vs. Fully-Hidden
Two distinct patterns are used throughout, and the choice between them is deliberate, not arbitrary:

items: **Visible but disabled** — the field renders for everyone, greyed out for those without edit rights. Used when it's reasonable for someone to _see_ their own status even if they can't change it (e.g. Soft Deleted, once visibility was extended to chapter admins).

**Fully hidden** — the field/section doesn't render in the DOM at all for unauthorized viewers. Used for genuinely sensitive things (Notes, Deceased, the core system-permission flags) where even knowing the field exists isn't appropriate for a regular member.

blocks.text: The Code

The QR holds `HC1:<card id>:<signature>`. The signature is the first 16 bytes of `HMAC-SHA256('card:<id>:<issued_at>')`, base64url (22 characters), keyed with `CARD_SECRET` from `.env`, or a key derived from `JWT_SECRET` when that's not set. So the code carries no personal information, the table holds nothing that makes a working code, and `card_lookup()` (compares with `hash_equals`) rejects anything made up or tampered with. A cancelled card's code still verifies but returns `status = cancelled`, so the door can say "cancelled card" rather than "not ours". **Changing `CARD_SECRET` (or `JWT_SECRET` when it's unset) cancels every card at once.**

items: A card is made the first time it's viewed (`issued_by` 0). Deceased and deleted members get none.

blocks.text: How the Gate Works
Set once, in your config file:

define('CCMPS_AUX_MODULE', 1); // full deployment
// or simply leave it undefined for a baseline-only deployment
Every aux-table section in `ccmpcrudcontact.php` and `viewccmp.php` is wrapped in:

<?php if (defined('CCMPS_AUX_MODULE') && CCMPS_AUX_MODULE == 1): ?>
    ... section content ...
<?php endif; ?>
With the constant undefined or 0, these sections don't just hide — they never render into the page at all, and no query for their data ever runs.

**One gotcha to remember when moving a field between a core and an aux section:** if a field lives in `ccmps_aux` but ends up displayed inside an otherwise-core section (this happened once with `hall_of_fame`, briefly placed in "Roles & Permissions"), it needs its _own_ inline `CCMPS_AUX_MODULE` check — wrapping just that one field, not the whole section — or a baseline deployment without `ccmps_aux` would try to display data from a table that doesn't exist.
Currently Aux-Gated Sections
Certificates & Ratings, Aircraft. (Additional Roles was removed entirely once its fields were renamed/relocated to core `ccmps` columns — see Known Issues.)
The Debug-Die() Landmine Pattern

The single most common bug found throughout this legacy codebase: a leftover debug line like `echo(1234); print_r($_SESSION); die();` sitting mid-function from whoever last debugged it. `die()` halts execution immediately — everything after it, including the actual save/redirect logic, silently never runs. We found and fixed this exact pattern independently in at least five different functions (`delrecord`, `undelrecord`, `removerecord`/`permdelete`, `ccmpsubmit`, `manage`) before recognizing it as a systemic pattern, then swept the entire ~8,000-line file and commented out all 334 remaining occurrences in one pass. **If you find a function that appears to "do nothing" or die unexpectedly, search it for a bare `die();` first — it is the most likely cause.**
Confirmed Real Bugs Found & Fixed (Reference List)

rows: **Session variable prefix mismatch — arguably the most severe bug found in this codebase.** Every permission check for system_admin/student_admin/subentity_admin checked the unprefixed session key, but `refreshmysessiondata()` (the actual login/session-population function) only ever sets the `ccmps_`-prefixed version. This meant every permission check involving these three roles silently evaluated to false for _every user, including genuine admins_ — not a visibility bug, a complete non-function. Caught only because a real system_admin logged in and found their own admin-only features inaccessible.
Every permission variable definition and every direct `$_SESSION[...]` check across all four files (`Ccmps.php`, `ccmpcrudcontact.php`, `viewccmp.php`, `manage.php`)

Added the `ccmps_` prefix throughout, matching the established (and correctly-used-elsewhere) convention already visible in `$_SESSION['ccmps_subentity']`/`$_SESSION['ccmps_subentity_role']`. **Separately confirmed and still unresolved:** `ccmp_admin`, `content_admin`, and `event_admin` are never assigned to any session variable anywhere in this file, under any naming — those three roles have never been functional at all, regardless of prefix. The actual login handler must live in a different module/controller not yet reviewed.
Object-syntax assignment on an array (`$data->prop = x` when `$data` is actually an array)
PHP throws a genuine fatal `Error` for property _assignment_ on an array (not a silent no-op, despite that being true for property _reads_). Converted to array syntax throughout.
Wrong table name used consistently, never actually tested
`ccmps_subentity_offices` used in 13 places — real table is `ccmps_subentity_roles`
Global rename. Lesson: a name appearing consistently throughout legacy code is not proof it's correct.

`_convert_to_user_friendly()` converted every boolean to the string `'Yes'`/`'No'` for view-page display, but the edit form's checkboxes used `!empty()` on the same field — and `!empty('No')` is `true`, since a non-empty string is always truthy regardless of content.
Removed the Yes/No conversion; the view page's own `vf_bool_row()` does its own direct truthy check instead.
Trongate doesn't reliably auto-populate parameters from URL segments; calling it via a plain link threw a fatal `ArgumentCountError`. Added a default value.

An accidentally-inserted extra `endif` prematurely closed the `CCMPS_AUX_MODULE` gate, leaving the file's real closing `endif` orphaned with nothing left to close — a fatal parse error. Always verify balance after restructuring conditional blocks, not just run `php -l` on the final result (which would have caught it, but checking structure explicitly is faster to debug).
Bulk-action dropdown silently pointed at the wrong table
`manage()` queried `subentities_bulk_actions`; a separate, similarly-named `ccmps_bulk_actions` table (the actually-intended one, per its name) had no effect when edited
Repointed the query. Caught by direct experience: someone edited the table expecting the dropdown to change, and nothing happened.
Real login never actually set the admin session flags it needed to

`successfullogin()` in `Welcome.php` — the assignments for `ccmps_student_admin`, `ccmps_system_admin`, and `ccmps_cms_admin` were commented out. A separate function, `refreshmysessiondata()`, did set them correctly, but nothing guaranteed it ran on every login. `ccmps_ccmp_admin` was never assigned at all, anywhere.
Uncommented and fixed the real login flow. `ccmp_admin` now gets assigned during login too. Caught directly: a real system_admin logged in and the flag still wasn't set.
Font size preference: three mutually incompatible conventions for the same session variable, plus a dead-code helper function

`$_SESSION['fontsize']` was set as a raw number in one place, a self-correcting 1/2/3 default in another, and converted to word-strings (`'Large'`/`'Medium'`/`'Small'`) via `switch` in a third — the last of which would silently break the numeric `<h#>` heading-level trick everywhere else read it as a number. Separately, `_get_font_sizes()` (called from 12+ places) referenced `$ccmp_id` before ever assigning it, so its entire database-lookup body was dead code the whole time.

Replaced entirely with the 5-element, per-user, database-backed system described in the Styling section above — not just the heading-level trick, but the single-value session variable itself. `_get_font_sizes()` kept as a documented no-op (12+ call sites still invoke it) rather than deleted; everything else — the old column, the AJAX handler, all three inconsistent assignment sites — removed outright.
Roster and directory never listed anyone

The views looped over `$rows`, but `currentroster()` / `currentdirectory()` pass `ccmpsrecs`. Views now loop over `$ccmpsrecs`; `$subentity_name` comes from `$_SESSION['subentity_name']`. Fixed 2026-10-19.
Roster, directory, export and master roster crashed or showed blank pilot columns

Any blank lookup id crashed `Model::get_where()` (now returns false for null). The queries read only `ccmps`, so aux fields (certificates, ratings, total time, call sign) were missing: they now use `_member_select()`, which joins `ccmps_aux` when `CCMPS_AUX_MODULE` is on. Old column names in the views were renamed (`member_no` → `ccmp_number`, `member_type` → `ccmp_type`, `chapter` → `subentity`, `chapter_role` → `subentity_role`, `other_faq_cert` → `other_faa_cert`); aircraft type and registration come from the first `ccmps_aircraft` row (`_first_aircraft()`). `special_event` and `no_address` no longer exist and print blank. Fixed 2026-10-19.

Adding a New Field — Step by Step

items: **Confirm the real column** — table, name, type. Never assume based on a similarly-named field elsewhere; several bugs in this module came from exactly that assumption.

**Decide the permission tier** — freely member-editable? Visible-but-disabled for non-admins? Fully hidden? Match it to an existing pattern in the RBAC tab rather than inventing a new one, unless the rule genuinely doesn't fit any existing tier.

**Add it to the form** (`ccmpcrudcontact.php`) — `cf_text()`/`cf_select()` for the appropriate table's section. If it's on `ccmps_aux`, make sure the section itself (or the field specifically) is wrapped in the `CCMPS_AUX_MODULE` check.
**Add it to the view** (`viewccmp.php`) — `vf_row()` for plain text, `vf_bool_row()` for a checkbox-style field, inside the matching tab.

**Add it to the server-side whitelist** (`Ccmps.php`, `ccmpsubmit()`) — this is the step most likely to be forgotten, and the one that actually matters for security. If it's restricted, add it to the appropriate strip list (`system_admin_only`, `broader_admin_only_text/bool`, or a new dedicated check if the rule doesn't fit an existing one) — **never** rely on the form's `disabled` attribute alone.
**Lint everything** — `php -l` on every file touched, every time. It's caught a real, otherwise-invisible bug (a malformed conditional block) more than once during this module's development.

blocks.text: Adding a New One-to-Many Child Table
The `ccmps_aircraft` table (a member can own/rent multiple aircraft) is the reference implementation for this pattern:

items: Fetch the full list in `_get_a_single_record()`, stored under its own key (e.g. `$data['aircraft_records']`) — not merged into the flat single-value `$data` array like everything else.

The form renders each existing record as its own editable row using array-indexed field names (`aircraft[0][make]`, `aircraft[1][make]`, ...), plus a couple of always-present blank rows for adding new ones — no JavaScript needed.

The save handler in `ccmpsubmit()` loops the submitted array: a row with a real `id` matching one this person actually owns gets updated (or deleted, if its delete checkbox was checked); a row with no `id` but real data gets inserted; a genuinely blank row is silently skipped. **Ownership is always re-verified server-side against the database** — never trust a submitted id at face value, or one member could edit/delete another member's records by guessing an id.

blocks.text: The Three-Tag System

Every document can carry one value from each of three independent tag lists, stored in `doctag1`, `doctag2` and `doctag3`. The **meaning** of each tag is set per client by renaming it, not by changing code:

Tag 1 is the "owner" tag: `dms_filelibrary_departments` rows each belong to a `doctag1` value. All three tags are filters on the manage page, and the active filters are shown above the list using the label constants.

**The manage page took the user's role from the URL.** `manage()` set `$_SESSION['filelibrary_rolename'] = segment(3);`, so any logged-in user (including a member) could open `dms-dmslibrary/manage/dmslibadmin` and list every document. Honcho's menu links have no role in the URL, which left the role empty and crashed the page with a 500 (`$sql` never set).

2026-10-11: `_get_dms_role()` works out the role on the server. **Members:** `ccmps_system_admin` → `dmslibadmin`, `ccmps_subentity_admin` (chapter admin) → `dmslibsubadmin` (own chapter's documents only), everyone else → `dmslibuser`. **Staff:** the same group → role lookup as the Honcho login, or `dmslibadmin` when `dms_lib_access` is 99; no group, or a role `manage()` has no view for (`dmslibastadmin`), → `dmslibuser`. blocks.text: Engine Additions PMS Depends On
Honcho's engine was modified to run Trongate 1.x code. To run PMS without breaking any of that, four small pieces were added on 2026-10-06:

items: `Trongate::make_model()` (`engine/Trongate.php`): if `modules/<module>/<Module>_model.php` exists, `$this->model` is that class; otherwise it is the shared legacy `Model`, as before. `Pm_model` extends the legacy `Model`, so it calls `$this->query_bind()` etc. directly; there is no `$this->db`.

`modules/validation/Validation.php`: `set_rules()` and `run()`. `run()` checks the CSRF token first (a bad token redirects to `BASE_URL`), then the rules: `required`, `min_length[n]`, `max_length[n]`, `numeric`, `integer`, `valid_email`, `valid_date`, `callback_<method>`. Errors go where `validation_errors()` reads them.
`block_url()` (`engine/tg_helpers/utilities_helper.php`): a validation callback calls `block_url('pm/team_check')` first so it 404s if visited as a page.
`Templates::error_404($data = [])`: made the argument optional so 404 pages stop crashing (affected the whole app, not just PMS).

What Is Not in Git

`.gitignore` keeps out: `.env`, database dumps (`ccmps.sql`, `ccmps_aux.sql`), user uploads (DMS and CMS library files, `public/uploads`, member photos in `modules/<module>/assets/<record id>/`), Inspinia's unused `Utils/` folder and zip, and backup copies (`* copy.php`, `*_old.php`, `*.last`, `legacy views/`, ...). The .env File

Secrets and anything that differs between installs live in `.env` in the project root. It is **never committed**; `.env.example` (committed) lists every setting with no real values. `config/env.php` reads it and provides `env('NAME', default)`; `config/config.php` and `config/database.php` use that. blocks.text: **Build from a folder, not a piped tar.** `.dockerignore` is ignored when the build context is piped in (`git archive | docker build -`). Build from a checkout: `docker build -t honcho ~/honcho`.
**Timezone:** the app runs on New York time (`docker/php.ini`). The droplet's own clock (logs, cron, the 4:00am update reboot) is on Central.
**Never put a key or password back into a committed file.** Add a new setting to `.env`, `.env.example` and the `env()` call in the config file. The root `.htaccess` refuses any request for `.env`.
Log in with an SSH key; there is no password login.
One-Time Setup on the Developer Mac

items: Create a key in the Terminal app (not through a `!` prompt, which can't answer questions): `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<your email>"`. Accept the default location and **set a passphrase**.

Copy the **public** key with `pbcopy < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` and add it in DigitalOcean (Settings → Security, or on the Create Droplet form). Never share `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (no extension); it is the private key.
Load the key into the Mac's SSH agent and Keychain once: `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.

blocks.text: ~/.ssh/config
Remembers the passphrase in Keychain and gives the droplet a short name, so `ssh bpa-honcho-01` connects:

Host *
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Host bpa-honcho-01
  HostName 159.223.185.25
  User eric
Accounts and SSH Settings on the Droplet

items: **`eric`** is the admin login: in the `sudo` group, same SSH key as above, and sudo needs no password (`/etc/sudoers.d/90-eric`). The passphrase-protected key is the protection; this matches DigitalOcean's and Ubuntu's own cloud images.

**Root cannot log in over SSH**, and **password logins are off** for everyone. Set in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-hardening.conf` (`PermitRootLogin no`, `PasswordAuthentication no`, `KbdInteractiveAuthentication no`). The `00-` prefix makes it win over DigitalOcean's `50-cloud-init.conf`, because sshd uses the first value it reads.
To check the live values: `sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei '^(permitrootlogin|passwordauthentication)'`.
To add another admin: create the user, add them to `sudo`, and put their **public** key in `/home/<user>/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

rows: `honcho-base`: inbound 22, 80, 443 from all IPv4 and IPv6; outbound default (all); applied to the droplet
Default `sshd` jail: bans an IP after repeated failed SSH logins

Staging Lock

Staging holds member-style data, so Caddy asks for a shared username and password (basic auth) on every page. The exception is `/welcome-api/*`: the mobile app sends its JWT login token in the same `Authorization` header that basic auth uses, and the API checks that token itself.

Some of these folders also hold committed files (dashboard images, the DMS user guide); the image keeps a copy, and `docker/entrypoint.sh` copies them back in on every start, never deleting an upload.

Views ask `ccmp_field_shown('department')` (`config/settings.php`); a field with no row is always shown. A hidden field isn't on the profile or the edit form, and saving keeps its stored value. To designate another field: add a `CCMPS_SHOW_<FIELD>` row by migration (category Member Fields) and wrap that field in `ccmp_field_shown()` in `viewccmp.php` and `ccmpcrudcontact.php`.

Adding a Setting

items: Write a migration in `database/migrations/` that inserts the row with `INSERT IGNORE` (so a re-run never overwrites a value changed on the screen): `title`, `label`, `settingvalue`, `category` (an existing tab or a new one), `input_type`, `options`, `rbac_function` (`edit_settings`, or `edit_financial_settings` for the Financial tab), `help`, `sort_order`.

In `config.php`: `define('MY_SETTING', setting('MY_SETTING', '<default>'));` - or `(int) setting(...)` for numbers and switches. Code outside `config.php` that needs it after a save can call `setting('MY_SETTING', <default>)` directly.

Input types: `text` (required, no < or >), `yesno`, `year`, `number` (`options` = range such as `6-64`), `fraction` (0-1), `url` (blank, `#` or https://), `phone`, `select` (`options` = `value=Label;value=Label`), `scheme`, `image`. blocks.text: Where It Is Going

Decided 2026-10-25: keep Inspinia for now rather than hand-writing a copy of it, and move gradually to **free Bootstrap 5 plus a small Honcho stylesheet** that keeps Inspinia's look and class names (`ibox`, `navbar-static-side`, ...), screen by screen as screens are touched. Bootstrap 5 is built on CSS variables, so the color schemes become real variables, and no theme licence is needed at the end. blocks.text: Never hard-code a client's name, wording, logo or color in a view. Use the constant (`SITENAME`, `CCMP`, `SUBENTITY`, `MAIN_LOGO`, the color constants).

items: **Every schema or data change is a migration** in `database/migrations/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>.sql`, with a header comment saying what and why. Never a `.sql` file in a module folder (it trips the engine's dev-mode check).

**Safe to run more than once:** `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, `INSERT IGNORE` on a unique key, `UPDATE ... WHERE` conditions that only match the first time. A re-run must never overwrite a value someone changed on a screen.
**Back up before running** (Mac: `~/honcho-backups/`, staging: `~/backups/`), and note the backup in the to-do list entry.
**Dropping a table** goes in its own script, run only after the change that replaced it has been checked (e.g. `2026-10-22-settings-phase1-drop-old-table.sql`).
**Test data is disposable; real data arrives by ETL** from the legacy database before UAT and go-live. A data fix made on the test data must be repeatable in the ETL (to-do: Legacy data load).

blocks.text: Queries: use `query_bind()` with named parameters for anything that comes from a user. Model rows are objects (`$row->field`); `$data` passed to a view is an array (`$data['field']`).

items: **Never assume a method is protected.** Many old `_check_function_permissions()` calls are commented out. Every public method that touches someone's data checks first.
**Member records:** call `Ccmps::_member_access($recid, view|edit|create|admin)` before anything else; `_deny_member_access()` when it says no (Security chapter).

**Other permissions:** Security Groups, `rbac_allowed('<module>', '<function>')` / `rbac_require()`. Member admin roles change only through `rbac_set_member_role()` and friends, never by writing the role columns.
**Who you are comes from the session** (`$_SESSION['tg_user_id']`, `ccmp_rec_id`), never from the URL or a form field.
**Every form that changes data is a POST with a session token** checked with `hash_equals` (e.g. `settings_token`, `cards_token`, `fontsize_token`). Links never change data.
**Whitelists:** only fields on an explicit list are saved (`ccmpsubmit()`'s field lists); an absent text field is left alone, an absent checkbox saves as 0.
**Methods starting with `_`** can't be reached from a URL: helpers are always `_`-prefixed.
**Log it:** changes that matter go to the Auditlog with `logevent()` (who, what, old value, new value).
**Text that goes straight into pages** (names, wording settings) can't contain `<` or `>`; everything else is escaped with `out()` / `htmlspecialchars()` when shown.

**Close and Cancel go back where the person came from**, not to the home page. The linking page passes `?return=<path>`; the screen also accepts the same-site referrer, keeps it in the session while the person stays on its pages, and accepts only a `module/method/args` path. Copy `Cards::_return_url()`.

**Per-person text sizes win.** Pages render with `$this->templates->inspinia($this->_with_fontsize_style($data))`. Never write a `font-size` inline on tabs, headings, labels, values or `.btn-label-text`; it overrides the member's choice. Use the existing classes instead.
**Site-specific CSS goes in `themes/inspinia/css/custom.css`** (linked with a version number so browsers fetch changes), never in the theme's own `style.css`.

**New libraries** go in their own pinned folder under `public/js/` with a README noting the version, licence and checksum (e.g. `qrcode-generator-1.4.4`), not into the theme and not from a CDN at run time.
**Buttons:** Save and Cancel sit together, same size; no debug text on labels (old line numbers like "128 Update" were removed).

**The top bar name** is `title_bar_name('member')` on member pages (BPA Member Portal) and `title_bar_name('admin')` on admin pages (BPA EMS): the words are System Settings > Organization (`SHORTSITENAME`, `SITENAME4`, `SHORTSITENAME2`), the colors the scheme's accent and primary. A new navbar calls the helper; never type the name into a view (old navbars said "SGAP EMS", another client's name, until 2026-10-27).
**Hiding a member field** a client doesn't want: a Member Fields switch, never commenting it out.

**Check it on screen.** For layout work, render the page in headless Chrome, screenshot and measure (`getBoundingClientRect`, `getComputedStyle`) at 1440 and 1280 wide before and after; a blind CSS fix once missed a third-party stylesheet that resized every button.
**Match the code around you:** naming, comment density and idioms of the file you're in. A simple change copies the existing pattern; a better approach is proposed, not slipped in.
**Call map:** each controller starts with a docblock listing its methods and the helpers each calls. Keep it current.
**Comments say why**, with the date when a rule was decided (e.g. "Lifetime members (2099) are always Current, decided 2026-10-22").

**Shared logic is a helper** in `engine/tg_helpers/` (e.g. `card_helper.php`, `rbac_helper.php`, `wallet_helper.php`) when more than one module needs it; settings helpers that config needs live in `config/settings.php`.
**Edit the live file**, never the backup copies (`* copy.php`, `*_old.php`, `x*` views).
**Engine is a v1/v2 Trongate hybrid:** `$this->model` is the generic v1 Model; stock v2 code may need adapting (CLAUDE.md, Controller conventions).

**When code changes, its docs change in the same piece of work:** the module's chapter here, the **Member Guide** (`docs/member-guide`) for anything every member sees, the **Administrator's Guide** (`docs/admin-guide`) for admin screens and setup walkthroughs, and `CLAUDE.md` for a new rule. Rebuilding a guide also refreshes its Help pages (`modules/help/content/<key>.json`); commit that file with it.
**`docs/todo.md`** is the list: add what's asked for "later", tick items off with the date and the commit.
**Syntax-check after editing:** `php -l` on PHP files, `node --check` on the guide's chapter files (a stray quote once stopped the guide from building).
**Commits** say what changed and why; never commit `.env` or key files (Google Wallet's key lives in `~/honcho-keys/`).
**Deploys** to staging: push, back up staging's database, pull and rebuild, run new migrations, then check the pages and logs. Always asked for first.
